title: Derived pushforward and pullback (finite coefficients)
statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be a Grothendieck abelian category and $g\colon Z\to Y$ a morphism of
schemes. Write $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal A)=D(\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal A))$ and
$D^+(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal A)$ for its bounded below part, and use the derived functors
of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. With $g_*$, $g^*$ as in
[def-sfb-finite-lower-star] and [def-sfb-finite-upper-star], define

$$
Rg_*:=R(g_*)\colon D(Z_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal A)\to D(Y_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal A),
$$

computed on K-injective resolutions, and its bounded below version
$R^+g_*\colon D^+(Z_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal A)\to D^+(Y_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal A)$,
computed on injective resolutions.

Assume moreover that $\mathcal A$ is closed symmetric monoidal with additive tensor
product and has functorial flat resolutions. Define

$$
Lg^*:=L(g^*)\colon D(Y_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal A)\to D(Z_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal A),
$$

computed on K-flat resolutions. Then:

1. $Lg^*\cong D(g^*)$, the functor induced levelwise by the exact functor $g^*$.
2. $Lg^*\dashv Rg_*$, and on bounded below categories $D^+(g^*)\dashv R^+g_*$.
3. For an open immersion $j$, the exact functors $j_!$ and $j^*$
   ([sk-def-sfb-finite-lower-shriek]) induce an adjunction $D(j_!)\dashv D(j^*)$, and
   likewise $D^+(j_!)\dashv D^+(j^*)$.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal C_X=\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal A)$ for $X=Z,Y$. These categories are Grothendieck abelian by [lem-sfb-proetale-sheaves-grothendieck]. Use the restriction functor $g_*$ of [def-sfb-finite-lower-star] and the adjunction $g^*\dashv g_*$ of [def-sfb-finite-upper-lower-star-adjunction]. The latter makes $g_*$ left exact: a cone to $g_*H$ represents, under the adjunction, exactly a cone from $g^*$ of the test object to $H$, so the limit universal property is preserved. In particular finite products and the zero object are preserved. Together with the restriction formula on maps this preserves addition, so $g_*$ is additive. Every complex of $\mathcal C_Z$ has a K-injective resolution by [lem-sfb-grothendieck-k-injective]. Applying the right-derived construction of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] to this additive functor defines $Rg_*$; on a quasi-isomorphism $K\to I$ with $I$ K-injective it is represented by $g_*I$.

source.place: Proof, first sentence; Stacks Tag 079P, theorem-K-injective-embedding-grothendieck, and derived.tex Tags 070K/070Y

proof.text: The category $\mathcal C_Z$ has enough injectives by [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives]. An object of $D^+$ has a representative $K$ with $H^i(K)=0$ for $i<a$. Replace $K$ by the complex zero below $a$, with $\operatorname{coker}(d_K^{a-1})$ in degree $a$ and $K^i$ in degrees $i>a$, using the differential induced by $d_K^a$. The canonical chain map from $K$ induces the same cohomology in degrees $i\geq a$ and has zero cohomology on both sides for $i<a$, so it is a quasi-isomorphism. For this bounded below representative, [lem-sc-bounded-below-injective-resolution-existence] supplies a quasi-isomorphism to a bounded below complex $I$ of injectives. Such an $I$ is K-injective by [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective]. Hence the formula of step 1 represents the restriction of $Rg_*$ by $g_*I$. Since the additive functor sends zero to zero, $g_*I$ is still zero below that bound. This defines $R^+g_*$ on $D^+$, computed by injective resolutions, and identifies it with the bounded below restriction of $Rg_*$.

source.place: Proof, first sentence, bounded below assertion; Mathlib CochainComplex.Plus.exists_quasiIso_injective and CochainComplex.isKInjective_of_injective

proof.text: Now impose precisely the stated closed symmetric monoidal, additive-tensor and functorial-flat-resolution hypotheses on $\mathcal A$. The existing node [def-sfb-finite-derived-pullback-iso] supplies the K-flat-computed left derived pullback and its natural isomorphism $Lg^*\cong D(g^*)$. Its hypotheses coincide with ours and its underived functor is [def-sfb-finite-upper-star]. The current exact-functor clause of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] is conditional on the respective derived-existence hypotheses. Here the cited [def-sfb-finite-derived-pullback-iso] has already supplied the K-flat-computed left derived pullback under exactly our coefficient hypotheses, so this condition is met. Exactness of $g^*$ is explicitly stated by [lem-sfb-finite-upper-star-exact]: applying $g^*$ to a K-flat resolution $P\to K$ gives a quasi-isomorphism $g^*P\to g^*K$, so the resolution formula agrees with the levelwise functor on every object. Thus item 1 uses the existing K-flat existence/comparison statement and does not assert an additional uncited functorial K-flat construction.

The functors just defined are the ones appearing in [def-sfb-finite-derived-adjunction]: K-flat-computed $Lg^*$ and K-injective-computed $Rg_*$. That node induces $Lg^*\dashv Rg_*$ from the underived adjunction. Its bounded below counterpart [def-sfb-finite-derived-adjunction-plus] gives $D^+(g^*)\dashv R^+g_*$ with the injective-resolution formula of step 2. Both nodes assume exactly the additional coefficient hypotheses now in force. These are the two adjunctions in item 2.

For an open immersion $j$, [sk-def-sfb-finite-lower-shriek] gives the exact extension by zero $j_!$ and its underived adjunction with $j^*$. The existing [def-sfb-finite-derived-extension-by-zero-adjunction] asserts exactness of both functors and the induced adjunction $D(j_!)\dashv D(j^*)$ for the same coefficient hypotheses. Applying the levelwise functors preserves lower bounds because their cohomology is obtained by applying the exact sheaf functors. The restriction statement [def-sfb-finite-derived-extension-by-zero-adjunction-plus] therefore supplies $D^+(j_!)\dashv D^+(j^*)$. This is item 3, with no constructibility or Tor-amplitude condition.

Steps 3-5 cite the five component nodes of this unit for items 1, 2 and 3. Their hypotheses are the item's monoidal hypotheses, and the blueprint proof itself says 'Item k is [...]', so this is not a relabelling. The route is valid: lem-sfb-finite-upper-star-exact belongs to sk-def-sfb-finite-pushforward-pullback, which the unit reaches transitively, and the other off-unit nodes are Mathlib leaves. No tool_uses are needed and no SGA source is cited. tools/review_split.py passes on the snapshot.
